text.p: Here are the highlights of stories in the Danish press on Friday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
--- A handful of demonstrators managed to prevent a South Korean freighter carrying genetically engineered soya beans from unloading its cargo in the harbour in Denmark's second largest city Aarhus.
--- Leading Danish banks have made huge profits selling four percent bonds worth more than 20 billion crowns during the last seven weeks, mainly to private investors.
--- Some 30 Danish export trucks caught in road blocks by protesting Greek drivers in Greece during the last week have been freed with the help of the Danish embassy in Athens.

--- After several months investigation police in southern Jutland near the Danish-German border have uncovered an organisation suspected of systematically smuggling Somalis into Denmark. Two members of the organisation were arrested with 24 Somalis hidden in a lorry about to be smuggled over the border.
--- 77 percent of all Danes show increasing mistrust of politicians' promises that state pensions will remain unchanged in future compared to 60 percent in 1995, a survey indicates.
